clue.text: Vehicle oil change initially not easy for her

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: a change of the word oil means its letters are rearranged
initially means the opening letters of the words not and easy are taken

explanation.surface: Someone finds that changing a car's oil is not an easy job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges OIL into OLI; 'initially' takes N and E from 'not easy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Caroline is a woman's name, and in this puzzle every 'her' clue defines a girl's name.

clue.text: Cleaner working for her

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British term for a cleaning lady
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is hired to work for some woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR (short for charwoman) is a British word for a hired cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Charon is taken as a woman's name here, a loose fit since in myth the ferryman is male.

clue.text: Stood up with girl — that's her!

parts.note: rose is the past tense of stand up, so stood up
Marie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman stood up beside a girl, pointing her out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemarie is a woman's first name, matching the puzzle's run of 'her' clues.

clue.text: Wood left with chief

parts.note: arch as an adjective means chief, as in arch-enemy

explanation.surface: A forest lies to the left of a leader's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch is a conifer whose timber is a well-known wood for building.

clue.text: Kiss permitted with jewellery

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A lover is allowed a kiss while wearing jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklet is a piece of jewellery worn closely round the neck.

clue.text: Edge round and aim roughly for her

indicators.note: round means the word for edge is turned about, read backwards

parts.note: a rim is an edge

indicators.note: roughly means the word aim is treated loosely, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An archer takes rough aim at the edge of the target, for some woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns RIM to MIR; 'roughly' rearranges AIM into IAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Miriam is a woman's name, the sister of Moses in the Bible.

clue.text: Mischievous child on donkey? I've become calm

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
an ass is a donkey
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A naughty child riding a donkey says he has finally calmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the IMP above the ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive means showing no emotion, unruffled and calm in manner.

clue.text: Adult insect comes from one male in the past

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A grown insect emerged from a single male long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the final, sexually mature stage of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Built railway for her

parts.note: made means built or constructed
a line is a railway line

explanation.surface: A railway was constructed for some woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeline is a woman's first name, one of this puzzle's theme of names.

clue.text: Remove — it's not concrete

definitions.meaning: to take something away or extract it, as a verb
as an adjective, existing only as an idea rather than as something solid

explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense means extract or remove, while the adjective describes ideas lacking physical existence.

clue.text: At university, drawback's getting a higher place

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford
read as draw back, the word draw turned backwards

explanation.surface: A student's handicap becomes a chance at a better position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' splits as 'draw back': DRAW reversed gives WARD. UP for 'at university' is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Upward means toward a higher place, the definition given loosely as a destination.

clue.text: Sticks up-self-satisfied

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: gums means sticks, as with glue

explanation.surface: A conceited person puts on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes someone excessively pleased with themselves, complacently self-satisfied.

clue.text: The room Philip chose has sex appeal

indicators.note: chose signals that a run of letters is picked out from the words room Philip

explanation.surface: The bedroom Philip picked has an erotic charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vigour or energy, and especially for sexual attractiveness.

clue.text: Bloom's.Law ruined soft fabric

indicators.note: ruined means the words are wrecked, their letters rearranged

parts.note: taken with its s as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal principle named after someone named Bloom spoils a soft material.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambswool is soft wool from young sheep, used for knitted fabric and garments.

clue.text: Shakespeare's forest takes time burning

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean woodland catches fire over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate, and in older use literally burning or glowing.

clue.text: The blaze I organised for her

indicators.note: organised means the letters of the words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone arranged a bonfire for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth is a woman's name, borne by two English queens.

clue.text: Flash information about record

indicators.note: about means the word for information goes around the other piece

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a list is a record of items

explanation.surface: A news bulletin is sent out about a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine or sparkle, so a verb close to flash or gleam.

clue.text: Stand-in assistant delayed by small guides

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker standing in for another
late means delayed
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A temporary helper turns up late with small instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Templates are patterns used as guides for cutting or shaping, or models for documents.

clue.text: Part of speech a man produces word for word

parts.note: a verb is one of the parts of speech
Tim is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man composes a sentence, choosing each part exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbatim means in exactly the same words as were used originally.

clue.text: Night is calm in capital of Germany

parts.note: even means calm, as in an even temper

indicators.note: capital of means the first letter of the word Germany

explanation.surface: Darkness falls calmly over a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Germany' tempts with BERLIN, but it means just G.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening is the close of day, and in loose use the night.

clue.text: Drink one for her

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic drink
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Someone buys a drink for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Gina is a woman's first name, short for Georgina or Regina.

clue.text: Article left with mother for her

parts.note: the is the definite article
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is left with Mum, for some woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a woman's first name, matching the theme of 'her' clues.

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
end means finish

indicators.note: confusion means the letters of at Brian in are jumbled

clue.text: Run into runic muddle

indicators.note: muddle means the letters of runic are mixed up

clue.text: Damaged pearl is not as colourful

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of pearl are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A damaged pearl loses some of its lustre.
explanation.definitionFit: Paler means lighter in shade, the comparative of pale, so less colourful.

clue.text: Previous head of house

definitions.meaning: the superior of a religious house such as a priory

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means earlier; the noun names a monk in charge of a religious house.

clue.text: Watch your heart

definitions.meaning: slang for a watch or clock, from its ticking
slang for the heart, which beats like a clock

explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal both for a timepiece and for the heart.

clue.text: Thin loam all over the place in New Zealand

indicators.note: all over the means the letters of thin loam are scattered and rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' reads as one phrase, but 'place' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is a city on the North Island of New Zealand.

clue.text: Thrust back silly hat for her

indicators.note: back means the word for thrust is read backwards

parts.note: to ram is to thrust forcefully

indicators.note: silly means the letters of hat are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shoves back a silly hat for a woman.

clue.text: Car sails off for her

indicators.note: off means the letters of car sails go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car goes skidding off the road for some woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarissa is a woman's first name, known from Richardson's novel.
